primary_outcome_name: Whole-body (total) lean body mass, change from baseline
primary_outcome_instrument_scale: DXA-derived total lean body mass, kg
primary_timepoint: Paper does not designate a single primary timepoint; it analyses 3 co-equal stages separately (T1-T2 = post 7-day wash-in; T2-T3 = post 12-week RT; T1-T3 = baseline to post-RT). The result reported first in the Abstract, taken here as the primary contrast per coding rule, is T1-T2 (post 7-day wash-in).
contrast_reported_primary: CrM supplement vs Control, whole-body LBM change, T1 (baseline) to T2 (post 7-day wash-in)
population_detail: Apparently healthy, untrained adults 18-50 years, BMI <=30 kg/m2, not meeting current physical activity guidelines (>=150 min/week moderate-intensity exercise), no RT in previous 12 months. Table 1 (p.5): Control n=33 (18F/15M), Supplement n=30 (16F/14M); age 31+/-8 (control) vs 30+/-8 (supplement) years.

published_estimate.quote: Results: After the 7-day wash-in, the supplement group gained 0.51 +/- 1.79 kg more lean body mass than the control group (p = 0.03). (Abstract, p.1). Body text (Section 3.1.1, p.6-7): 'After the CrM wash-in period without exercise, there was a significant difference between groups for changes in total LBM favouring the supplement group (p = 0.03; Supplement: Delta 0.51 +/- 1.26 kg; Control: Delta 0 +/- 1.20 kg; Figure 4).' Note: the Abstract's '+/- 1.79' for the 0.51 kg figure does not match the +/-1.26 kg SD given for the supplement arm's own change in Section 3.1.1 -- an internal inconsistency in the paper; no explicit CI or SE for the between-group difference itself is reported anywhere in the main text.

B_covariate_list: Absolute (whole-body/segmental) LBM at the start of the respective stage, used as covariate in the linear regression model for that stage (i.e. baseline-of-stage LBM only; no other covariates such as age/sex/BMI included in the primary LBM model).
registration_id: ACTRN12622000040763 (Australia New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry)
data_availability_statement: Data Availability Statement: The anonymised data collected are available as open data via the Open Science Framework (https://osf.io/4pu2t/).

registry_check.issues: Our registry.csv row uses data_file 'Desai-Data-LBM-segmental.xlsx' with outcome_var legs_post1/legs_pre (segmental LEG lean mass), with the note 'Ganzkoerper-Magermasse nicht im Deposit, nur Segmente'. This is INCORRECT: whole-body (total) LBM IS present in the deposit, but in the OTHER file, 'Desai-Data-LBM.xlsx' (sheet 'Data'), which has columns dxa_leanmass_kg_pre, dxa_leanmass_kg_post_1, dxa_leanmass_kg_post_2 (and derived lbm_change_post_1/2/3) -- this is exactly the whole-body LBM outcome that the paper actually reports as its main result (Figure 4, Sections 3.1.1-3.1.3). The registry should be updated to point to Desai-Data-LBM.xlsx with outcome_var dxa_leanmass_kg_post_1 (T2, wash-in) or dxa_leanmass_kg_post_2 (T3, post-RT) vs baseline_var dxa_leanmass_kg_pre, rather than the segmental leg columns in Desai-Data-LBM-segmental.xlsx. arm_control='Control' matches the paper's 'Control' group label correctly. Separately: the Abstract states 'Sixty-three... participants were randomised', which equals the n analysed in Table 1 (33 control + 30 supplement), but the Results text separately states 'One male from the CrM group withdrew after the baseline assessment... and was not included in the analysis', implying the true number randomised may have been 64, with the Abstract's '63' actually describing the baseline-analysed sample rather than the randomised sample -- flagged as an internal ambiguity, not resolved here. Also: this trial is described as part of a larger RCT registered under a different title ('The influence of the gut microbiome on resistance training-based skeletal muscle hypertrophy in healthy individuals', ACTRN12622000040763); the registered primary outcome of that larger trial may not be LBM at all -- this could not be verified from the paper text alone (would require checking the ANZCTR entry itself, out of scope here) and is a candidate outcome-switching concern for the reporting audit.

analysis_method_quote: 2.3.5. Statistical Analyses (p.6): 'Normality and equal variances were assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk and Levene's tests, respectively. Independent t-tests were performed to determine whether baseline anthropometric and physical activity values were different between groups. Differences in whole-body and segmental LBM change between groups were analysed separately across the 3 stages of the intervention: 7-day non-exercise wash-in (T1 to T2); 12-week RT intervention only (T2 to T3); wash-in and RT intervention (T1 to T3). A linear regression model was used to analyse the differences in LBM changes between groups for each stage, with absolute LBM from the beginning of the respective stage used as a covariate to adjust for baseline differences... The Wilcoxon rank-sum test and generalised linear model (GLM) were used instead of the independent t-test and the linear regression model, respectively, when data were not normal or variances were unequal... Significance was set at p <= 0.05 and 95% confidence intervals were used. All analyses were conducted on R Studio version 4.3.2 using the base stats, and emmeans (1.10.0) and SimplyAgree (0.1.2) packages.'
notes: DEPOSIT CHECK (openpyxl column headers, both files in deposit/): (1) Desai-Data-LBM-segmental.xlsx, sheet 'Data', 48 columns, ONLY segmental variables: arms_*, legs_*, trunk_* (pre/post1/post2, raw and kg, plus change_1/2/3) -- no whole-body LBM column. (2) Desai-Data-LBM.xlsx, sheet 'Data', 43 columns, INCLUDES whole-body variables: record_id, group, sex, birthdate, age, height_stadiometer, scale_bodyweight_pre, bmi_pre, dxa_fat_percent_pre, dxa_totalmass_kg_pre, dxa_fatmass_kg_pre, dxa_leanmass_kg_pre, dxa_fatfreemass_kg_pre, diet variables, scale_bodyweight_post_1, bmi_post_1, dxa_fat_percent_post_1, dxa_totalmass_kg_post_1, dxa_fatmass_kg_post_1, dxa_leanmass_kg_post_1, dxa_fatfreemass_kg_post_1, bw_scale_change_post_1, lbm_change_post_1, diet_post_1, ... post_2 equivalents ..., lbm_change_post_2, lbm_change_post_3. CONCLUSION: whole-body (total) lean body mass -- the paper's actual outcome of interest -- IS available in the deposit, in Desai-Data-LBM.xlsx (dxa_leanmass_kg_pre / _post_1 / _post_2, and pre-computed lbm_change_post_1/2/3), contrary to the registry note that it is 'not in the deposit, only segments'. The registry's segmental-only assessment appears to have been based on inspecting only Desai-Data-LBM-segmental.xlsx and missing the second file. Design note: this is a 3-timepoint, single-blind (participant not blinded to allocation is unclear; described only as part of a 'single-blind, controlled, randomised trial') RCT nested within a larger trial on gut microbiome and RT-induced hypertrophy; both arms undergo the identical 12-week RT program (supervised by 'tertiary qualified exercise physiologists', p.6) after the wash-in, so the RT component is not the randomised contrast -- only CrM vs no-CrM is. No a priori sample-size/power calculation was performed for the LBM outcome itself ('Given that the effect size of the gut microbiota on LBM changes was unknown, an a priori power analysis was not conducted... The intended sample size of 33 per group... included a potential attrition rate of 10%').
